translations.literal: (From the Biography of Liu Wensou in the Brief Account of the Eastern Capital: When the Khitan entered the capital, Wensou feared being taken north with them and with Chief Academician Zhang Yun sought to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: (Brief Account of the Eastern Capital, Biography of Liu Wensou: When the Khitans entered the capital, Wensou feared being taken north and with Chief Academician Zhang Yun sought to resign.

sentences.zh: 契丹主怒，欲黜為縣令。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler was angry and wished to demote him to county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler was angry and wished to demote him to county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 趙延壽曰：「學士不稱職而求解者，罷之可也。

translations.literal: Zhao Yanshou said: "When an academician is unfit for office and seeks release, dismissal is enough."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanshou said, "When an academician is unfit and asks to leave, dismissal suffices."

translations.idiomatic: He was not demoted.)〉

sentences.zh: 乾祐初，授吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyou he was appointed vice minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianyou he was vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 自誅史宏肇後，京城士庶，連甍恐悚，允每朝退，即宿於相國寺僧舍。

translations.literal: After Shi Hongzhao was executed, gentry and commoners in the capital were in continuous terror; after each court session Yun lodged in a monk's cell at Xiangguo Temple.
translations.idiomatic: After Hongzhao's execution the capital lived in terror; after each court session Yun slept in a monk's cell at Xiangguo Temple.

sentences.zh: 及北軍入京師，允匿於佛殿藻井之上，墜屋而卒，時年六十五。

translations.literal: When the northern army entered the capital, Yun hid in the coffered ceiling of the Buddha hall, fell through the roof, and died at age sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern army entered the capital he hid in the Buddha hall ceiling, fell through, and died at sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 子鸞，仕皇朝為太常少卿。

translations.literal: His son Luan served the Song court as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His son Luan served the Song as vice director of imperial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 任延皓，并州人也。

translations.literal: Ren Yanhao was a native of Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yanhao was from Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 業術數風雲之事。

translations.literal: He mastered numerology and the arts of wind and cloud omens.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered numerology and divination by wind and cloud.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖在太原重圍時，高祖最為親要，延皓以本業請見，高祖甚加禮遇。

translations.literal: When the Jin Gaozu was in the heavy siege at Taiyuan he was among those most intimate and trusted; Yanhao asked audience by his profession and was greatly honored.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Gaozu was besieged at Taiyuan, Yanhao was among his most trusted; he sought audience by his arts and was greatly honored.

sentences.zh: 晉天福初，延皓授太原掾，尋改交城、文水令，皆高祖慰薦之力也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin Tianfu Yanhao was appointed Taiyuan clerk, soon changed to magistrate of Jiaocheng and Wenshui—all by the Gaozu's comforting recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianfu he was Taiyuan clerk, then magistrate of Jiaocheng and Wenshui on Gaozu's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 高祖鎮太原，延皓多言外事，出入無間，高祖左右皆憚之。

translations.literal: When the Gaozu governed Taiyuan, Yanhao spoke much of external affairs and came and went without interval; those at the Gaozu's side all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu governed Taiyuan, Yanhao spoke constantly of outside affairs and came and went freely; even his close attendants feared him.

sentences.zh: 在文水聚斂財賄，民欲陳訴，延皓知之。

translations.literal: At Wenshui he amassed wealth by extortion; the people wished to complain and Yanhao learned of it.
translations.idiomatic: At Wenshui he extorted wealth; when the people meant to complain, he learned of it.

sentences.zh: 一日，先誣告縣吏結集百姓，欲劫縣庫。

translations.literal: One day he first falsely reported that county clerks had gathered the people to plunder the county treasury.
translations.idiomatic: One day he first accused the county clerks of rallying the people to loot the treasury.

sentences.zh: 高祖怒，遣騎軍並擒縣民十數，族誅之，冤枉之聲，聞於行路。

translations.literal: The Gaozu was angry and sent cavalry who together seized more than ten county people and executed their clans; cries of injustice were heard on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent cavalry who seized a dozen county people and executed their clans; cries of injustice filled the roads.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，累官至殿中監，恃寵使氣，人望而畏之，雖宰輔之重，延皓視之蔑如也。

translations.literal: When the Gaozu took the throne, Yanhao rose to palace director; relying on favor he was overbearing and men feared him at sight; even chancellors he regarded with contempt.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne Yanhao rose to palace director; arrogant with favor, he was feared at sight; even chancellors he treated with contempt.

sentences.zh: 劉崇在河東，日常切齒。

translations.literal: Liu Chong at Hedong daily gnashed his teeth at him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chong at Hedong gnashed his teeth at him daily.

sentences.zh: 及魏王承訓薨，歸葬太原，令延皓擇葬地，時有山岡僧謂劉崇曰：「魏王葬地不吉，恐有重喪。

translations.literal: When Prince Wei Cheng Xun died and was buried at Taiyuan, Yanhao was ordered to choose the burial ground; a hill monk then told Liu Chong: "The prince's burial ground is inauspicious; I fear repeated mourning."
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Wei Cheng Xun died and was buried at Taiyuan, Yanhao chose the site; a hill monk told Liu Chong, "The burial ground is ill-omened; I fear further mourning."

sentences.zh: 」未幾，高祖崩，崇以僧言奏之，乃配流延皓於麟州。

translations.literal: Before long the Gaozu died; Chong memorialized the monk's words and Yanhao was banished to Lin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Gaozu died; Chong reported the monk's words and Yanhao was banished to Lin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 路由文水，市民擲瓦毆罵甚眾，吏人救之僅免。

translations.literal: Passing Wenshui, townspeople threw tiles and cursed him in great numbers; clerks barely saved him.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Wenshui, townspeople pelted him with tiles and cursed him; clerks barely saved him.

sentences.zh: 既至貶所，劉崇令人殺之，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Reaching his place of exile, Chong had him killed and his household confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: At his place of exile Chong had him killed and his property confiscated.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：李崧仕唐、晉之兩朝，聳伊、臯之重望，考其器業，無忝臺衡。

translations.literal: The historian says: Li Song served the two dynasties of Tang and Jin, towering with the heavy repute of Yi and Gao; examining his capacity and achievement, he did not disgrace the highest office.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Li Song served Tang and Jin, bearing the weight of Yi and Gao; in capacity and achievement he did not disgrace the highest office.

sentences.zh: 會多僻之朝，被參夷之戮，人之不幸，天亦難忱。

translations.literal: Meeting a perverse age, he suffered execution that extinguished his clan—man's misfortune, and Heaven too is hard to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: In a crooked age he suffered execution that wiped out his clan—man's misfortune, and Heaven is hard to fathom.

sentences.zh: 逢吉秉蛇虺之心，竊夔、龍之位，殺人不忌，與國俱亡。

translations.literal: Fengji bore a viper's heart and usurped the place of Kui and Long, killing without scruple and perishing with the state.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji bore a viper's heart, usurped Kui and Long's place, killed without scruple, and perished with the state.

sentences.zh: 李崧之冤血未銷，逢吉之梟首斯至，冥報之事，安可忽諸！

translations.literal: Li Song's unjust blood was not yet dry when Fengji's displayed head arrived—how can matters of hidden retribution be neglected!
translations.idiomatic: Song's unjust blood was not dry when Fengji's head was displayed—hidden retribution must not be ignored!

sentences.zh: 自李鏻而下，凡數君子者，皆踐履朝行，彰施帝載，國華邦直，斯焉在哉！

translations.literal: From Li Lin downward, these several gentlemen all trod the court ranks and shone in the imperial record—the state's flower and the state's integrity are here!
translations.idiomatic: From Li Lin down, these gentlemen walked the court ranks and shone in the imperial record—national grace and integrity dwell here!

sentences.zh: 惟延皓之醜行，宜乎不得其死矣。

translations.literal: Only Yanhao's vile conduct—fitting that he should not die a natural death.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yanhao's vile conduct—fitting that he died as he did.
